words.ex_cn: 博物馆下个月将展览古钱币。
words.en: To exhibit something means to show it in a public place so that people can go to see it. It can also mean to show a particular quality, ability, or type of behavior.

words.ex: The red light signifies stop.
words.ex_cn: 红灯表示停止。
words.en: If an event, a sign, or a symbol signifies something, it is a sign of that thing or represents that thing.

words.ex: The symbol x denotes an unknown number.
words.ex_cn: 符号 x 表示一个未知数。
words.en: If one thing denotes another, it is a sign or indication of it.

words.ex: The dark clouds indicate rain.
words.ex_cn: 乌云表明要下雨了。
words.en: If one thing indicates another, the first thing shows that the second is true or exists.

words.ex: He will rectify the mistake tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他明天会纠正这个错误。
words.en: If you rectify something that is wrong, you change it so that it becomes correct or satisfactory.

words.ex: He tried to justify his mistake by saying he was tired.
words.ex_cn: 他试图以自己累了为由来证明自己的错误是正当的。
words.en: To justify something means to show or prove that it is reasonable, necessary, or correct.

words.ex: The teacher will notify the students about the test.
words.ex_cn: 老师会通知学生们关于考试的事。
words.en: If you notify someone of something, you officially inform them about it.

words.tr:
n. 塑料；
adj. 塑料的；
words.ex: The bottle is made of plastic.
words.ex_cn: 这个瓶子是塑料做的。
words.en: A plastic is a material which is produced from oil by a chemical process and which is used to make many objects. It is light in weight and does not break easily.

words.ex: The beer left foam on the top of the glass.
words.ex_cn: 啤酒在杯子顶部留下了一层泡沫。
words.en: Foam is a mass of small bubbles that are formed in or on a liquid.

words.ex: They used cement to build the wall.
words.ex_cn: 他们用水泥建造了这堵墙。
words.en: Cement is a powdery substance which is mixed with water and used for sticking things together or for making very hard surfaces.

words.ex: He bought a porcelain cup at the market.
words.ex_cn: 他在市场上买了一个瓷杯。
words.en: A hard, white, translucent ceramic that is made by firing a pure clay and then glazing it.

words.tr:
n. 陶瓷制品；陶瓷器；
adj. 陶质的；制陶的；
words.ex: He bought a ceramic bowl at the market.
words.ex_cn: 他在市场上买了一个陶瓷碗。
words.en: Ceramic is a hard material that is made by baking clay or similar substances at high temperatures. It is used to make things such as tiles, dishes, and statues.

words.tr: n. 陶器；制陶手艺；陶器作坊；
words.ex: He makes pottery in his backyard studio.
words.ex_cn: 他在后院的工作室制作陶器。
words.en: Objects such as pots, dishes, and vases that are made out of clay and then baked at high temperatures to make them hard.

words.ex: The river is contaminated by factory waste.
words.ex_cn: 这条河被工厂废料污染了。
words.en: To contaminate something means to make it impure or polluted by contact or mixture with something unclean or harmful.

words.ex: The factory pollutes the river.
words.ex_cn: 工厂污染了这条河。
words.en: To pollute water, air, or land means to make it dirty and dangerous to live in or to use, especially with poisonous chemicals or waste.

words.tr:
n. 毒药；毒物；
v. 毒害；
words.ex: The snake's poison can kill quickly.
words.ex_cn: 蛇的毒药能迅速致死。
words.en: A poison is a substance that causes harm or death if it is swallowed, absorbed, or breathed in. It can also refer to something that has a very harmful effect on something else.

words.ex: He practices his religion every Sunday.
words.ex_cn: 他每周日都实践自己的宗教信仰。
words.en: Religion is the belief in and worship of a superhuman controlling power, especially a personal God or gods.

words.ex: The temple is a sacred place for believers.
words.ex_cn: 这座寺庙对信徒来说是神圣的地方。
words.en: Something that is sacred is considered to be holy or connected with God or a god.

words.tr: adj. 世俗的；非宗教的；长期的
words.ex: He lives a secular life without religion.
words.ex_cn: 他过着没有宗教的世俗生活。
words.en: Secular activities, attitudes, or things have no connection with religion.

words.ex: God is almighty and can do anything.
words.ex_cn: 上帝是全能的，能做任何事。
words.en: The Almighty is used to refer to God. It can also describe something that has very great power or influence.

words.ex: He preaches kindness every Sunday.
words.ex_cn: 他每周日都宣扬仁爱。
words.en: If you preach, you give a talk on a religious or moral subject during a religious service.

words.tr: n. （宗教等的）仪式；例行习惯；
words.ex: The village holds a ritual every spring to pray for good weather.
words.ex_cn: 这个村庄每年春天都举行一个仪式，祈求好天气。
words.en: A ritual is a religious service or other ceremony which involves a series of actions performed in a fixed order.

words.ex: It is a taboo to speak his name in this village.
words.ex_cn: 在这个村子里，提到他的名字是禁忌。
words.en: A taboo is a social or religious custom prohibiting or restricting a particular practice or forbidding association with a particular person, place, or thing.

words.ex: He is a scientist of great renown.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位享有盛誉的科学家。
words.en: Renown is the state of being known and talked about by many people because of your achievements, qualities, or actions.

words.tr:
n. 名声；名誉；名望
v. 认为；以为
words.ex: He is of good repute in his town.
words.ex_cn: 他在镇上声誉很好。
words.en: The opinion generally held of someone or something; the state of being regarded in a particular way.

words.ex: He has a good reputation for honesty.
words.ex_cn: 他以诚实著称。
words.en: The opinion that people have about someone or something because of what has happened in the past.

words.tr:
v. 传播；扩散；散布；
n. 传播；蔓延；范围；
words.ex: The virus spread quickly through the city.
words.ex_cn: 病毒在城市中迅速传播。
words.en: To spread something means to open it out or arrange it over a place or surface, so that all of it can be seen or used easily.

words.ex: Blood circulates in the body.
words.ex_cn: 血液在体内循环。
words.en: To move or cause to move continuously or freely through a closed system or area.

words.ex: The police dispersed the crowd.
words.ex_cn: 警察驱散了人群。
words.en: If a crowd of people disperses or is dispersed, it breaks up and the people go in different directions.

words.ex: The wind scatter the leaves everywhere.
words.ex_cn: 风把树叶吹得四处分散。
words.en: To scatter means to throw or drop things over a wide area in an irregular way, or to cause a group of people or animals to move apart in different directions.

words.tr:
v. 弥漫；
adj. 分散的；
words.ex: Smoke began to diffuse through the room.
words.ex_cn: 烟开始弥漫在整个房间里。
words.en: If something such as knowledge or information is diffused, or if it diffuses, it is made known over a wide area or to a lot of people.

words.ex: The smell of bread permeate the kitchen.
words.ex_cn: 面包的香味弥漫了整个厨房。
words.en: If something permeates a place, it spreads throughout it.

words.tr: v. 使浸透；使湿透；使满；使饱和
words.ex: The sponge will saturate if you pour too much water.
words.ex_cn: 如果你倒太多水，海绵会吸满。
words.en: To saturate something means to make it completely wet, or to fill it completely with something so that no more can be added.

words.ex: He is a conservative man who likes old traditions.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个喜欢古老传统的保守男子。
words.en: A conservative person or group is one that does not like changes or new ideas, especially in politics or religion.

words.ex: He follows the orthodox religious practices.
words.ex_cn: 他遵循正统的宗教习俗。
words.en: Orthodox beliefs, methods, or systems are ones which are accepted or used by most people.

words.tr:
n. 刻板印象；陈规老套
v. 对…存有成见；把…模式化
words.ex: He broke the stereotype that boys cannot cry.
words.ex_cn: 他打破了男孩不能哭的刻板印象。
words.en: A stereotype is a fixed general image or set of characteristics that a lot of people believe represent a particular type of person or thing.

words.ex: He used a cliche to describe the sunset.
words.ex_cn: 他用一个陈词滥调来形容日落。
words.en: A cliché is an idea or phrase that has been used so much that it is no longer interesting or effective.

words.ex: This phone is outdated and doesn't work well.
words.ex_cn: 这部手机过时了，用起来不好。
words.en: If you describe something as outdated, you mean that you think it is old-fashioned and no longer useful or relevant to modern life.

words.ex: The bread is stale because it was left out too long.
words.ex_cn: 面包不新鲜了，因为它放得太久。
words.en: If food or air is stale, it is no longer fresh and therefore unpleasant.

words.tr: adj. 渴望的；热心的；敏锐的；
words.ex: He is keen to learn English.
words.ex_cn: 他渴望学习英语。
words.en: If you are keen on doing something, you very much want to do it. If you are keen that something should happen, you very much want it to happen.

words.ex: The doctor said the patient needs urgent care.
words.ex_cn: 医生说病人需要紧急治疗。
words.en: If something is urgent, it needs to be dealt with as soon as possible.

words.ex: He listens to music to relax.
words.ex_cn: 他听音乐来放松。
words.en: If you relax or if something relaxes you, you feel more calm and less worried or tense.

words.tr:
n. 奖励；报酬；
v. 奖励；回报；
words.ex: He got a reward for winning the contest.
words.ex_cn: 他因赢得比赛而得到了奖励。
words.en: Something given or received in return for a deed or service rendered.

words.tr: adj. 严重的；严厉的；非常困难的；
words.ex: The storm caused severe damage to the houses.
words.ex_cn: 这场风暴对房屋造成了严重的破坏。
words.en: If something is severe, it is very bad or very serious.

words.ex: He copes with stress by walking every day.
words.ex_cn: 他通过每天散步来应对压力。
words.en: To cope with a problem or task means to deal with it successfully.

words.tr: adv. 否则；在其他方面；除此之外；
words.ex: Hurry up, otherwise you'll be late.
words.ex_cn: 快点，否则你会迟到的。
words.en: in circumstances different from those present or considered; or else

words.ex: He is aware of the danger.
words.ex_cn: 他意识到危险。
words.en: If you are aware of something, you know about it.

words.ex: The team consists of five players.
words.ex_cn: 这个团队由五名球员组成。
words.en: If something consists of particular things or people, it is made up of them.

words.tr: adj. 可怜的；悲哀的；差劲的；令人生厌的
words.ex: The little dog looked pathetic in the rain.
words.ex_cn: 那只小狗在雨中看起来很可怜。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as pathetic, you mean that they are sad and weak or inadequate, and you feel contempt or pity for them.

words.ex: He will consult a doctor for his headache.
words.ex_cn: 他将咨询医生治疗他的头痛。
words.en: to seek information or advice from someone, especially someone who is an expert in a particular field

words.ex: I will arrange a meeting for tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 我将为明天安排一次会议。
words.en: If you arrange an event or meeting, you make plans for it to happen.

words.ex: He lost all his property in the fire.
words.ex_cn: 他在火灾中失去了所有财产。
words.en: Something owned; a possession.

words.ex: The teacher gave extra praise to satisfy the students.
words.ex_cn: 老师给予额外的表扬来使学生满意。
words.en: If someone or something satisfies you, they give you enough of what you want or need to make you pleased or contented.

words.tr:
n. 妥协；
v. 危及；
words.ex: They reached a compromise after hours of talk.
words.ex_cn: 经过数小时的讨论，他们达成了妥协。
words.en: A compromise is an agreement between two people or groups in which each side gives up some of the things they want so that both sides are happy at the end.

words.ex: A problem arose during the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 会议中出现了一个问题。
words.en: If a situation or problem arises, it begins to exist or people start to become aware of it.

words.tr: n. 车辆；交通工具；媒介；
words.ex: The vehicle stopped at the red light.
words.ex_cn: 这辆车在红灯前停了下来。
words.en: A vehicle is a machine such as a car, bus, or truck which has an engine and is used to carry people or goods from place to place.

words.tr: n. 四轮运货马车；敞篷货车；
words.ex: The farmer used a wooden wagon to carry crops.
words.ex_cn: 农夫用一辆木制四轮运货马车运送庄稼。
words.en: A wagon is a vehicle with four wheels, usually pulled by horses or oxen, used for transporting goods.

words.ex: He drives a red van to work.
words.ex_cn: 他开一辆红色的货车去上班。
words.en: A van is a road vehicle used for transporting goods or people, usually larger than a car but smaller than a truck.

words.ex: The locomotive pulled the train down the track.
words.ex_cn: 机车拉着火车沿着轨道行驶。
words.en: A locomotive is a powered rail vehicle used for pulling trains.

words.ex: The train has a sleeping compartment for passengers.
words.ex_cn: 火车上有一个供乘客休息的隔间。
words.en: A compartment is a separate section or part of something, especially a space in a vehicle that is separated from other spaces.

words.ex: The trucks stop at the depot to load goods.
words.ex_cn: 卡车在仓库停靠以装载货物。
words.en: A depot is a place where large amounts of raw materials, manufactured goods, or equipment are stored until they are needed.

words.tr: v. 使屈辱；使丢脸；使蒙羞
words.ex: He tried to humiliate her in front of the class.
words.ex_cn: 他试图在全班面前羞辱她。
words.en: To humiliate someone means to make them feel ashamed or stupid, especially in front of other people.

words.tr:
n. 滥用；虐待；辱骂；
v. 滥用；虐待；辱骂；
words.ex: The abuse of power led to many problems.
words.ex_cn: 权力的滥用导致了许多问题。
words.en: Abuse is the improper usage or treatment of a thing, often to unfairly or improperly gain benefit. Abuse can come in many forms, such as physical or verbal maltreatment, injury, assault, violation, rape, unjust practices, crimes, or other types of aggression.

words.ex: He felt shame for lying to his mother.
words.ex_cn: 他因为对母亲撒谎而感到羞愧。
words.en: A painful feeling of humiliation or distress caused by the consciousness of wrong or foolish behavior.

words.ex: He felt the stigma of being unemployed.
words.ex_cn: 他感受到了失业的耻辱。
words.en: A stigma is a strong feeling of disapproval that most people in a society have about something, especially when this is unfair.

words.tr:
adj. 警觉的；警惕的；
n. 警报；
v. （使）警惕；（使）戒备；
words.ex: The alert guard noticed the strange movement.
words.ex_cn: 这位警觉的警卫注意到了奇怪的动静。
words.en: If you are alert, you are paying full attention to things around you and are able to deal with anything that might happen.

words.tr: adj. （言行）谨慎的；不显眼的；朴素的
words.ex: He was discreet about his personal life.
words.ex_cn: 他对自己的私生活很低调。
words.en: If you are discreet, you are polite and careful in what you do or say, because you want to avoid embarrassing or offending someone.

words.tr: adj. 一丝不苟的；缜密的
words.ex: He is meticulous about checking his homework.
words.ex_cn: 他仔细检查作业。
words.en: If you describe someone as meticulous, you mean that they do things very carefully and with great attention to detail.

words.ex: He was wary of strangers who offered free gifts.
words.ex_cn: 他对那些提供免费礼物的陌生人保持谨慎。
words.en: If you are wary of something or someone, you are cautious because you do not know much about them and you believe they may be dangerous or cause problems.

words.tr:
adj. 深思熟虑的；故意的；
v. 深思熟虑；
words.ex: He made a deliberate choice to quit his job.
words.ex_cn: 他深思熟虑后决定辞去工作。
words.en: If you do something that is deliberate, you planned or decided to do it beforehand, and so it happens on purpose rather than by chance.

words.ex: Fish reproduce in the river.
words.ex_cn: 鱼在河里繁殖。
words.en: To produce something again; to make a copy of something.

words.tr:
v. 交配繁殖；饲养；
n. 品种；
words.ex: The farmers breed cows to get more milk.
words.ex_cn: 农民让奶牛交配繁殖以获得更多牛奶。
words.en: If you breed animals or plants, you keep them for the purpose of producing more animals or plants with particular qualities, in a controlled way.

words.ex: The virus can propagate quickly among people.
words.ex_cn: 这种病毒可以在人群中迅速传播。
words.en: To propagate something means to spread it and encourage more people to believe in it or support it.

words.ex: The scientist created a clone of the sheep.
words.ex_cn: 科学家克隆了一只羊。
words.en: A clone is an organism or cell produced asexually from one ancestor or stock, to which they are genetically identical.

words.ex: She sells handmade handicraft at the market.
words.ex_cn: 她在市场上出售手工制品。
words.en: Handicraft refers to activities where useful and decorative objects are made completely by hand or by using only simple tools.

words.tr: n. 工艺；手艺；行业；航空器；
words.ex: The craft of pottery takes years to learn.
words.ex_cn: 陶艺工艺需要多年才能掌握。
words.en: Skill in making things by hand; the skilled practice of a practical occupation; the skilled production of decorative or functional objects.

words.tr: n. 人工制品；手工艺品；加工品
words.ex: The museum has an ancient artifact.
words.ex_cn: 博物馆里有一件古代文物。
words.en: An artifact is an object that is made by a person, especially something of historical or cultural interest.

words.tr: n. 雕刻（术）；雕塑品；雕刻品；
words.ex: He made a beautiful sculpture from clay.
words.ex_cn: 他用黏土做了一件精美的雕刻。
words.en: Sculpture is the art of making two- or three-dimensional representative or abstract forms, especially by carving stone or wood or by casting metal or plaster.

words.ex: He carved the meat with a sharp knife.
words.ex_cn: 他用一把锋利的刀切开了肉。
words.en: To carve means to cut into a hard material in order to produce an object, design, or inscription.

words.ex: The diamond has many smooth facets.
words.ex_cn: 这颗钻石有许多光滑的小平面。
words.en: A particular aspect or feature of something.

words.ex: She made an embroidery of a flower on the pillow.
words.ex_cn: 她在枕头上绣了一朵花。
words.en: Embroidery is the craft of decorating fabric or other materials using a needle to apply thread or yarn. It may also incorporate other materials such as pearls, beads, quills, and sequins.

words.tr:
n. 最小值；
adj. 最小量的；
words.ex: The minimum of the function is 5.
words.ex_cn: 这个函数的最小值是5。
words.en: The minimum is the smallest or least amount possible or allowed.

words.ex: The noise will diminish after midnight.
words.ex_cn: 午夜后噪音会减少。
words.en: If something diminishes, or if something diminishes it, it becomes reduced in size, importance, or intensity.

words.tr:
adj. 次要的；轻微的；小的；小调的；
n. 未成年人；
words.ex: The mistake was a minor error.
words.ex_cn: 这个错误是一个小错误。
words.en: A minor is a person who is under the age at which they legally become an adult.

words.tr:
adj. 零下的；负的；
n. 缺点；
prep. 减去；
words.ex: The temperature is minus ten degrees Celsius.
words.ex_cn: 气温是零下十摄氏度。
words.en: A minus is a mathematical symbol that represents subtraction or a negative quantity.

words.tr:
n. 最大限度；最大量；
adj. 最大极限的；最多的；
words.ex: The maximum of the crowd is 100 people.
words.ex_cn: 人群的上限是100人。
words.en: The greatest or highest amount possible or attained.

words.ex: The government wants to eradicate poverty.
words.ex_cn: 政府希望消灭贫困。
words.en: To eradicate something means to get rid of it completely.

words.ex: He omitted the last word in the sentence.
words.ex_cn: 他省略了句子中的最后一个词。
words.en: If you omit something, you do not include it in an activity or piece of work, deliberately or accidentally.

words.ex: We must eliminate the waste to protect the environment.
words.ex_cn: 我们必须消除浪费以保护环境。
words.en: To eliminate something, especially something you do not want or need, means to remove it completely.

words.ex: The government decided to abolish the old law.
words.ex_cn: 政府决定废除这项旧法律。
words.en: If someone in authority abolishes a system or practice, they formally put an end to it.

words.ex: He will cancel the meeting tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他明天会取消会议。
words.en: If you cancel something that has been arranged, you stop it from happening. If you cancel an order for goods or services, you tell the person or organization supplying them that you no longer wish to receive them.

words.ex: He will delete the old file.
words.ex_cn: 他会删除那个旧文件。
words.en: To delete something means to remove it or erase it.

words.tr: adj. 灭绝的；熄灭的；绝种的；
words.ex: The dodo is an extinct bird.
words.ex_cn: 渡渡鸟是一种灭绝的鸟。
words.en: If a species of animals or plants is extinct, it no longer has any living members, either in the world or in a particular place.

words.ex: He extinguished the fire with water.
words.ex_cn: 他用水把火扑灭了。
words.en: To extinguish a fire or a light means to stop it burning or shining.

words.ex: The sun makes the puddle evaporate quickly.
words.ex_cn: 太阳使水坑很快蒸发。
words.en: If a liquid evaporates, or if something evaporates it, it changes from a liquid state to a gas, because its temperature has increased.

words.tr: v. 销声匿迹；突然消失；
words.ex: The magic trick made the coin vanish.
words.ex_cn: 这个魔术让硬币销声匿迹了。
words.en: If someone or something vanishes, they disappear suddenly or in a way that cannot be explained.

words.ex: The committee will convene tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 委员会明天将召开会议。
words.en: If someone convenes a meeting or conference, they arrange for it to take place. They can also be said to convene when they meet.

words.ex: The two roads converge at the town center.
words.ex_cn: 这两条路在镇中心交汇。
words.en: If roads or lines converge, they meet or join at a particular place.

words.ex: He will assemble the toy for his son.
words.ex_cn: 他将为儿子组装玩具。
words.en: If people assemble or if someone assembles them, they come together in a group, usually for a particular purpose such as a meeting.

words.tr:
n. 总计；集合体
adj. 合计的；总的
v. （使）聚集；聚合；总计为
words.ex: The aggregate of all sales this month is $50,000.
words.ex_cn: 本月所有销售额的总计是5万美元。
words.en: An aggregate is a number of things or people that are considered as a group or a whole.

words.ex: People congregate in the park on weekends.
words.ex_cn: 人们在周末聚集在公园里。
words.en: To congregate means to come together in a group or crowd.

words.ex: People gather in the square for the festival.
words.ex_cn: 人们在广场上聚集庆祝节日。
words.en: If people gather somewhere, or if someone gathers people somewhere, they come together in a group.

words.tr:
v. 集合起来；振作；复苏
n. 集会
words.ex: The crowd rallied to support their team.
words.ex_cn: 人群聚集起来支持他们的球队。
words.en: A rally is a large public meeting that is held in order to show support for something such as a political party or a sports team. It can also mean to come together again in order to continue fighting or arguing after a defeat or a period of confusion.

words.ex: The judge will summon him tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 法官明天将传唤他。
words.en: If you summon someone, you order them to come to you.

words.tr:
n. 进口；重要性；
v. 进口；
words.ex: The country increased its import of oil last year.
words.ex_cn: 去年这个国家增加了石油的进口。
words.en: To bring in (goods or services) from a foreign country for sale or use.

words.tr:
n. 输出；出口；
v. 输出；出口；
words.ex: This country is a big export of wheat.
words.ex_cn: 这个国家是小麦的大输出国。
words.en: To send goods to another country for sale.

words.tr: n. 关税；税率；（旅馆、饭店等的）价目表
words.ex: The government raised the tariff on imported cars.
words.ex_cn: 政府提高了进口汽车的关税。
words.en: A tariff is a tax that a government collects on goods coming into a country.

words.tr:
v. 征收；征税；征募
n. 征兵；征税
words.ex: The government will levy a new tax next month.
words.ex_cn: 政府下个月将征收一项新税。
words.en: To levy means to impose or collect a tax, fee, or fine. It can also refer to the act of enlisting or drafting individuals into military service.

words.tr: v. 导航；应付（复杂情况）；
words.ex: He uses a map to navigate the city.
words.ex_cn: 他用地图来导航这座城市。
words.en: To navigate is to plan and direct the route or course of a ship, aircraft, or other form of transport, especially by using instruments or maps.

words.tr:
n. 乘船游览；航游；
v. 乘船游览；航游；
words.ex: We went on a cruise around the Mediterranean Sea.
words.ex_cn: 我们乘船游览了地中海。
words.en: To sail about in an area without a precise destination, especially for pleasure.

words.tr:
n. 护送；护航；护卫
v. 护航；护送
words.ex: The army sent a convoy to protect the trucks.
words.ex_cn: 军队派出护送队保护卡车。
words.en: A convoy is a group of vehicles or ships traveling together, typically accompanied by armed troops, warships, or other vehicles for protection.

words.ex: The submarine sailed quietly under the sea.
words.ex_cn: 潜水艇在海底安静地航行。
words.en: A submarine is a type of ship that can travel underwater. It is used primarily by the military for defense purposes, but some are used for scientific research.

words.ex: He paints on a canvas with oil colors.
words.ex_cn: 他用油画颜料在帆布上作画。
words.en: A strong, coarse unbleached cloth made from hemp, flax, cotton, or a similar yarn, used to make items such as sails and tents and as a surface for oil painting.

words.ex: The small town has a maritime history.
words.ex_cn: 这个小镇有着海洋历史。
words.en: Relating to the sea, especially in relation to seaborne trade or naval matters.

words.ex: The marine birds fly over the sea.
words.ex_cn: 这些海鸟在海面上飞翔。
words.en: Marine is used to describe things relating to the sea or to the ships and boats which sail on it.

words.ex: The extra chair is redundant because we have enough seats.
words.ex_cn: 这把额外的椅子是多余的，因为我们已经有足够的座位了。
words.en: If you are made redundant, your employer tells you to leave because your job is no longer necessary or because there is no more work for you.

words.ex: He was reluctant to leave his home.
words.ex_cn: 他不愿意离开家。
words.en: If you are reluctant to do something, you are unwilling to do it and hesitate before doing it, or do it slowly and without enthusiasm.

words.ex: The teacher intervened when the students argued.
words.ex_cn: 当学生们争吵时，老师进行了干涉。
words.en: If you intervene in a situation, you become involved in it and try to change it.

words.ex: The store made an inventory of all the products.
words.ex_cn: 商店对所有商品做了一份清单。
words.en: An inventory is a detailed list of all the items in a place.

words.ex: The company's revenue increased last year.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司的收入去年增加了。
words.en: Revenue is the income that a company, organization, or government receives regularly.

words.ex: He has a masculine voice and strong build.
words.ex_cn: 他声音低沉，身材强壮。
words.en: Having qualities or appearance traditionally associated with men.

words.ex: She has a feminine voice.
words.ex_cn: 她的声音很女性化。
words.en: having qualities or an appearance traditionally associated with women, especially delicacy and prettiness.

words.tr: adj. 母亲的；母性的；母系的；
words.ex: Her maternal love kept the family strong.
words.ex_cn: 她的母爱让家庭保持坚强。
words.en: Maternal feelings or actions are typical of a kind, loving mother.

words.ex: The forest is a virgin land, untouched by humans.
words.ex_cn: 这片森林是未开发的土地，从未被人类触及过。
words.en: A virgin is someone who has never had sexual intercourse. It can also describe something that is in its original pure or natural condition and has not been touched or changed by people.

words.tr:
n. 接触（的机会或权利）；进入；通道；
v. 获取；使用；接近；
words.ex: Students need access to the library.
words.ex_cn: 学生需要有接触图书馆的机会。
words.en: If you have access to a building or other place, you are able to enter it or use it.

words.ex: They accused him of stealing the money.
words.ex_cn: 他们指控他偷了钱。
words.en: If you accuse someone of doing something wrong or dishonest, you say or tell them that you believe that they did it.

words.tr:
n. 过量；过度；超过；
adj. 多余的；
words.ex: The excess of sugar in his diet caused health problems.
words.ex_cn: 他饮食中糖分过量导致了健康问题。
words.en: An excess of something is a larger amount than is needed, allowed, or usual.

words.tr: v. 暗指；（间接）提到；影射
words.ex: He alluded to the problem without naming it.
words.ex_cn: 他暗示了这个问题，但没有点明。
words.en: To allude to something means to mention it in an indirect way.

words.ex: The appendix contains extra data for the report.
words.ex_cn: 附录包含了报告的额外数据。
words.en: An appendix is a section at the end of a book that contains additional information. It can also refer to the small tube attached to the large intestine in the human body, known as the vermiform appendix.

words.ex: There was an array of people at the concert.
words.ex_cn: 音乐会上人山人海。
words.en: An array of different things or people is a large number or wide range of them.

words.ex: The police arrested the thief last night.
words.ex_cn: 警察昨晚逮捕了那个小偷。
words.en: If the police arrest you, they take charge of you and take you to a police station, because they believe you may have committed a crime.

words.tr:
v. 记录；准确地描述；俘虏；吸引；
n. 抓捕；
words.ex: The camera can capture the moment clearly.
words.ex_cn: 相机可以清晰地记录下这一瞬间。
words.en: To capture someone or something means to catch them, especially after a chase.

words.ex: The two companies will merge next year.
words.ex_cn: 这两家公司明年将合并。
words.en: To combine or unite to form a single entity.

words.ex: She combines flour and water to make dough.
words.ex_cn: 她把面粉和水混合在一起做面团。
words.en: To combine means to join or merge two or more things together to form a single entity.

words.ex: The two parties formed a coalition to win the election.
words.ex_cn: 这两个政党联合起来以赢得选举。
words.en: A coalition is a temporary alliance for combined action, especially of political parties forming a government.

words.ex: The rain and the thunder happened in conjunction.
words.ex_cn: 雨和雷声同时发生。
words.en: A conjunction is a word that is used to connect clauses or sentences or to coordinate words in the same clause.

words.ex: The car stopped at the junction.
words.ex_cn: 汽车在交叉路口停了下来。
words.en: A junction is a place where two or more things, especially roads or railways, come together.

words.tr: v. 由于保险丝烧断而电路不通；熔接；结合；
words.ex: The light went out because the fuse blew.
words.ex_cn: 灯灭了，因为保险丝烧断了。
words.en: A fuse is a safety device consisting of a strip of wire that melts and breaks an electric circuit if the current exceeds a safe level. As a verb, it means to join or blend to form a single entity.

words.tr: v. 使相混；使联结；交际
words.ex: He mingled the two colors to make a new one.
words.ex_cn: 他把两种颜色混合在一起，创造出一种新颜色。
words.en: If things such as sounds, smells, or feelings mingle, they mix or combine with each other, or if people mingle, they talk to each other at a social event.

words.ex: This is a genuine diamond.
words.ex_cn: 这是一颗真正的钻石。
words.en: If something is genuine, it is real and exactly what it appears to be.

words.tr:
v. 伪造；假装；冒充；
adj. 假的；冒充的；伪造的；
words.ex: He faked a signature to get the money.
words.ex_cn: 他伪造了一个签名来拿到钱。
words.en: If something is fake, it is not real, genuine, or true, but is made to appear so.

words.ex: The flowers in the garden are artificial.
words.ex_cn: 花园里的花是人造的。
words.en: Made or produced by human beings rather than occurring naturally, especially as a copy of something natural.

words.ex: He complains about the loud noise every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天都抱怨噪音太大。
words.en: To express dissatisfaction, pain, or resentment, usually because of a particular situation or someone's actions.

words.tr:
adv. 相同地；相像地；
adj. 相同的；相像的；
words.ex: They dress alike.
words.ex_cn: 他们穿得一样。
words.en: If two or more things are alike, they are similar in some way.

words.ex: This is a good instance of teamwork.
words.ex_cn: 这是一个团队合作的好例子。
words.en: An instance is a particular example or case of something.

words.tr:
n. 对照；反差；对立；
v. 对比；和...形成对照；
words.ex: The contrast between light and dark is clear in the photo.
words.ex_cn: 这张照片中明暗的对照很明显。
words.en: A contrast is a great difference between two or more things which is clear when you compare them.

words.ex: He remarked that the weather was nice.
words.ex_cn: 他评论说天气很好。
words.en: If you remark that something is the case, you say that it is the case.

words.tr: v. 逐渐削弱；暗中损害；
words.ex: Constant criticism can undermine your confidence.
words.ex_cn: 不断的批评会逐渐削弱你的信心。
words.en: To undermine something means to weaken it or make it less effective, often in a gradual or sneaky way.

words.tr:
n. 冒险事业；商业冒险；投机；
v. 冒险；投机；
words.ex: He started a new venture in technology.
words.ex_cn: 他创办了一项新的科技冒险事业。
words.en: If you venture somewhere, you go somewhere that might be dangerous. If you venture a question or statement, you say it in an uncertain way because you are afraid it might be stupid or wrong.

words.ex: The accident was a serious incident.
words.ex_cn: 那场事故是一起严重事件。
words.en: An incident is an event that is either unpleasant or unusual.

words.tr:
n. 海峡；渠道；河床；频道；
v. 引导；
words.ex: The English Channel separates England from France.
words.ex_cn: 英吉利海峡将英格兰与法国分隔开。
words.en: A channel is a television station and the programs that it broadcasts. A channel is also a method or system that people use to send information, goods, etc. to each other.

words.ex: The restaurant caters to vegetarians.
words.ex_cn: 这家餐厅满足素食者的需求。
words.en: To cater means to provide food and drink at an event, often as a business service, or to provide what is needed or wanted by a particular person or group.

words.ex: The children are eager to open their presents.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们渴望打开他们的礼物。
words.en: If you are eager to do or have something, you want to do or have it very much.

words.ex: He uses an efficient way to solve math problems.
words.ex_cn: 他用一种高效的方法解决数学问题。
words.en: If something or someone is efficient, they are able to do tasks successfully, without wasting time or energy.

words.tr:
n. 同事；（组织的）会员；家伙；同胞；
adj. 同类的；同事的；
words.ex: He works as a fellow with Dr. Smith in the lab.
words.ex_cn: 他在实验室里与史密斯博士一起工作，是他的同事。
words.en: A fellow is a man or boy. In British English, a fellow is also a member of certain academic societies.

words.tr: n. 一阵强劲的气流；爆炸；
words.ex: A blast of cold wind hit the window.
words.ex_cn: 一阵冷风击中了窗户。
words.en: A blast is a sudden loud noise or a strong gust of wind. It can also refer to an explosion or the act of blowing something up. As a verb, it means to explode or to criticize severely.

words.ex: He plays violin in a local orchestra.
words.ex_cn: 他在一个本地管弦乐队中拉小提琴。
words.en: An orchestra is a large group of musicians who play a variety of different instruments together. Orchestras usually play classical music.

words.tr: n. 音乐会；演奏会；一致；和谐；
words.ex: We went to a concert last night.
words.ex_cn: 我们昨晚去听了音乐会。
words.en: A concert is a performance of music by one or more musicians or singers, which usually takes place in the evening.

words.ex: The drummer changed the tempo of the song.
words.ex_cn: 鼓手改变了这首歌的拍子。
words.en: The speed at which a piece of music is played or the rate or speed of motion or activity.

words.ex: The guitarist played a C major chord.
words.ex_cn: 吉他手弹了一个C大和弦。
words.en: A chord is a group of three or more musical notes played together.

words.ex: The baby smiled at the sweet melody.
words.ex_cn: 宝宝听到了甜美的旋律，笑了。
words.en: A melody is a sequence of single notes that is musically satisfying.

words.ex: The rhythm of the music made everyone dance.
words.ex_cn: 音乐的节奏让所有人都跳起了舞。
words.en: A rhythm is a regular series of sounds or movements.

words.ex: He flipped through the album with old photos.
words.ex_cn: 他翻看着装满旧照片的相册。
words.en: An album is a collection of several pieces of music, songs, or photographs that are intended to form a single item.

words.tr: n. 磁带；录音带；胶带；带子；
words.ex: He recorded the song on a tape.
words.ex_cn: 他把这首歌录在磁带上。
words.en: A tape is a narrow strip of plastic or other material that is used for recording sound or pictures, or for sticking things together.

words.ex: The clown entertains the children with funny tricks.
words.ex_cn: 小丑用滑稽的把戏娱乐孩子们。
words.en: To entertain someone means to amuse or interest them, for example by telling them stories or jokes, or by playing music for them.

words.tr: n. 娱乐；消遣；休闲活动
words.ex: Reading books is his favorite recreation.
words.ex_cn: 读书是他最喜欢的消遣。
words.en: Recreation is activity that you do for enjoyment or amusement when you are not working.

words.ex: Reading books is his favorite pastime.
words.ex_cn: 读书是他最喜欢的消遣。
words.en: A pastime is something that you do because you enjoy it or are interested in it, rather than as a job.

words.ex: He reads books in his leisure.
words.ex_cn: 他在空闲时间读书。
words.en: Leisure is the time when you are not working and you can relax and do things that you enjoy.

words.ex: He went to the casino to play poker.
words.ex_cn: 他去赌场玩扑克。
words.en: A casino is a building where people can gamble by playing games of chance or betting on events.

words.tr: n. 美容院；美发厅；沙龙
words.ex: She goes to the salon to get her hair cut.
words.ex_cn: 她去理发店剪头发。
words.en: A salon is a gathering of people under the roof of an inspiring host, held partly to amuse one another and partly to refine the taste and increase the knowledge of the participants through conversation.

words.ex: He bought a lottery ticket last week.
words.ex_cn: 他上周买了一张彩票。
words.en: A lottery is a type of gambling game in which people buy numbered tickets. Several numbers are then chosen, and the people who have those numbers on their tickets win a prize.

words.ex: He plays hockey every weekend.
words.ex_cn: 他每个周末打冰球。
words.en: Hockey is a sport played on ice or on a field, in which two teams try to hit a small hard object called a puck or a ball into the other team's goal using long curved sticks.

words.tr:
v. 摔跤；扭斗；奋力对付
n. 摔跤；角力；扭斗
words.ex: He tries to wrestle the dog away from the trash.
words.ex_cn: 他试图把狗从垃圾桶旁拉开。
words.en: To engage in a physical contest, typically involving grappling and trying to throw or immobilize the opponent, or to struggle with a difficult problem or decision.

words.tr:
adv. 向前；前进；
v. 促进；转交；
adj. 向前的；前进的；
words.ex: He walked forward to meet the teacher.
words.ex_cn: 他向前走去见老师。
words.en: If you move or look forward, you move or look in a direction that is in front of you. In British English, you can also say that you are looking forward to something that is going to happen.

words.tr:
adv. 向下地；
adj. 向下的；
words.ex: The leaves fell downward slowly.
words.ex_cn: 树叶慢慢向下飘落。
words.en: Moving or leading towards a lower place or level

words.ex: The ship sailed inward toward the harbor.
words.ex_cn: 船向港口内航行。
words.en: Directed or moving towards the inside; relating to the inside or inner part of something.

words.tr:
adj. 精瘦的；精简的；不景气的；
v. 倾斜；倚靠；
words.ex: The dog is lean and fast.
words.ex_cn: 这只狗精瘦而敏捷。
words.en: If you lean in a particular direction, you bend your body in that direction. If you lean on or against someone or something, you rest against them so that they partly support your weight. If you describe someone as lean, you mean that they are thin but look strong and healthy. If you describe a period of time as lean, you mean that it is a time when people have very little of something, especially money.

words.tr:
v. （使）倾斜；（使）偏向
n. 倾斜；企图
words.ex: The boy tilt the cup and spill the water.
words.ex_cn: 男孩把杯子倾斜，水洒了出来。
words.en: If you tilt an object or if it tilts, it moves into a sloping position with one end or side higher than the other.

words.ex: His sadness manifested in his quiet eyes.
words.ex_cn: 他的悲伤表现在他安静的眼神中。
words.en: To manifest something means to show it clearly and visibly.

words.ex: The red hat was conspicuous in the crowd.
words.ex_cn: 那顶红帽子在人群中非常显眼。
words.en: Something that is conspicuous is very obvious or easy to notice.

words.ex: It is obvious that he is tired.
words.ex_cn: 很明显他很累。
words.en: If something is obvious, it is easy to see or understand.

words.tr: adj. 值得注意的；显著的；
words.ex: This result is noteworthy because it changes our understanding.
words.ex_cn: 这个结果值得注意，因为它改变了我们的理解。
words.en: If you describe something as noteworthy, you mean that it is interesting, significant, or important enough to deserve attention or to be noticed.

words.tr: adj. 突出的；杰出的；显著的；
words.ex: He is a prominent scientist in the field of medicine.
words.ex_cn: 他是医学领域的一位突出的科学家。
words.en: Someone or something that is prominent is important and well-known, or is positioned in a way that makes them easily seen or noticed.

words.ex: It is apparent that he is tired.
words.ex_cn: 很明显他很累。
words.en: If something is apparent, it seems to be true, although you cannot be certain that it is.

words.tr: adj. 杰出的；尚未处理的；
words.ex: He is an outstanding student who always gets top grades.
words.ex_cn: 他是一名杰出的学生，总是取得最高分。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as outstanding, you think that they are very remarkable and impressive.

words.ex: He gave an explicit answer to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题给出了明确的答案。
words.en: Something that is explicit is expressed or shown clearly and openly, without any attempt to hide anything.

words.ex: The two colors are distinct.
words.ex_cn: 这两种颜色有区别。
words.en: If something is distinct, it is easily seen, heard, or understood.

words.ex: The difference between the two colors is subtle.
words.ex_cn: 这两种颜色之间的区别很微妙。
words.en: Something that is subtle is not immediately obvious or noticeable, but is rather indirect or understated.

words.ex: His silence was an implicit apology.
words.ex_cn: 他的沉默是一种含蓄的道歉。
words.en: Something that is implicit is expressed in an indirect way.

words.tr:
n. 潜力；
adj. 潜在的；
words.ex: The young athlete shows great potential.
words.ex_cn: 这位年轻运动员展现出巨大的潜力。
words.en: If you say that someone or something has potential, you mean that they have the necessary abilities or qualities to become successful or useful in the future.

words.tr: v. 使合格；使具有资格；
words.ex: He studied hard to qualify for the job.
words.ex_cn: 他努力学习以获得这份工作的资格。
words.en: To qualify means to meet the necessary conditions or standards to be eligible for something or to perform a particular role.

words.ex: We need to quantify the results of the experiment.
words.ex_cn: 我们需要量化实验的结果。
words.en: If you try to quantify something, you try to calculate how much of it there is.

words.ex: The quantity of water in the bottle is small.
words.ex_cn: 瓶子里的水量很少。
words.en: A quantity is an amount that you can measure or count.

words.ex: The teacher supervises the students during the experiment.
words.ex_cn: 老师在实验期间指导学生。
words.en: If you supervise an activity or a person, you make sure that the activity is done correctly or that the person is doing a task or behaving correctly.

words.tr: v. 主持；指挥；担任会议主席
words.ex: He presides over the meeting every Monday.
words.ex_cn: 他每周一主持会议。
words.en: To preside means to be in charge of a formal meeting, ceremony, or other event.

words.ex: The police used surveillance to watch the building.
words.ex_cn: 警察使用监视来观察那栋大楼。
words.en: The careful watching of a person or place, especially by the police or army, because of a crime that has happened or is expected.

words.ex: Honesty is a good trait.
words.ex_cn: 诚实是一种好的特性。
words.en: A trait is a particular characteristic, quality, or tendency that someone or something has.

words.ex: He has a streak of kindness that makes everyone like him.
words.ex_cn: 他有一种善良的性情，让每个人都喜欢他。
words.en: A streak is a long thin mark that is a different colour from the surfaces next to it. It can also refer to a period of time during which a particular kind of behaviour or activity is consistently shown.

words.ex: The company has a famous trademark on its logo.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司在其标志上有一个著名的标记。
words.en: A trademark is a recognizable sign, design, or expression which identifies products or services of a particular source from those of others.

words.tr: n. 含酒精的饮料；酒精；
words.ex: He drank alcohol at the party.
words.ex_cn: 他在派对上喝了含酒精的饮料。
words.en: Alcohol is a colourless liquid that can make you drunk, and which is used in medicines, cleaning products, and other substances.

words.ex: They drank champagne at the wedding.
words.ex_cn: 他们在婚礼上喝了香槟。
words.en: Champagne is an expensive French white wine with bubbles in. It is often drunk to celebrate something.

words.ex: The scientist created a cocktail of chemicals for the experiment.
words.ex_cn: 科学家为实验配制了一种化学混合物。
words.en: A cocktail is a mixed drink typically made with a combination of alcoholic beverages and other ingredients such as fruit juices, syrups, or cream.

words.ex: He drank a glass of ale at the pub.
words.ex_cn: 他在酒吧喝了一杯麦芽酒。
words.en: Ale is a type of beer that is brewed using a warm fermentation method, resulting in a sweet, full-bodied and fruity taste.

words.tr:
n. 一小口；
v. 呷；啜；小口喝；
words.ex: He took a sip of water.
words.ex_cn: 他喝了一小口水。
words.en: To drink something slowly by taking small amounts into your mouth.

words.tr: adj. 清醒的；严肃的；素淡的；
words.ex: He stayed sober after drinking only water.
words.ex_cn: 他只喝了水，保持清醒。
words.en: If you are sober, you are not drunk. If you are sober, you are serious and thoughtful.

words.ex: The magic trick will astonish you.
words.ex_cn: 这个魔术会让你惊讶。
words.en: If something or someone astonishes you, they surprise you very much.

words.ex: The magic show amazed the children.
words.ex_cn: 魔术表演让孩子们感到惊奇。
words.en: To amaze someone means to surprise them very much.

words.ex: The loud noise stunned him.
words.ex_cn: 巨大的噪音让他震惊了。
words.en: To stun someone means to shock or surprise them very much.

words.ex: He eats an apple every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上吃一个苹果。
words.en: A round fruit with firm, white flesh and a green, red, or yellow skin.

words.ex: The violent news appalls her.
words.ex_cn: 这起暴力新闻令她震惊。
words.en: to fill with horror or dismay; shock deeply

words.tr: n. 城河；壕坑; n. （Foss）人名；（德、英、法、西、瑞典）福斯
words.ex: The castle is surrounded by a deep foss.
words.ex_cn: 城堡被一条深城河环绕。
words.en: A fossilized remnant or trace of an organism from a past geological age.

words.tr:
v. 惊异于；惊异；
n. 令人惊异的人（或事）；
words.ex: I marvel at how fast she runs.
words.ex_cn: 我惊异于她跑得有多快。
words.en: If you marvel at something, you express your great surprise, wonder, or admiration.

words.ex: The movie was incredible.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影太棒了。
words.en: If you describe something or someone as incredible, you like them very much or are impressed by them, because they are extremely or unusually good.

words.ex: He edits the school newspaper every week.
words.ex_cn: 他每周编辑校报。
words.en: To prepare written material for publication by correcting, condensing, or otherwise modifying it.

words.tr:
n. 社论；
adj. 编辑的；
words.ex: The newspaper published an editorial about climate change.
words.ex_cn: 报纸发表了一篇关于气候变化的社论。
words.en: An editorial is an article in a newspaper which gives the opinion of the editor or publisher on a topic or item of news.

words.ex: He will proofread the letter before sending it.
words.ex_cn: 他在发送这封信之前会校对。
words.en: To read and mark corrections on a text before it is published.

words.ex: He compiles data from many surveys.
words.ex_cn: 他汇编来自许多调查的数据。
words.en: To compile means to collect information from different places and arrange it in a book, report, or list.

words.ex: He looked at the catalog to find the book.
words.ex_cn: 他翻看目录来找那本书。
words.en: A catalog is a list of things, such as the goods you can buy from a particular company, the objects in a museum, or the books in a library.

words.tr: phrase. 卡片目录（用于图书馆中按卡片索引图书的系统）
words.ex: He found the book using the card catalogue.
words.ex_cn: 他通过卡片目录找到了这本书。
words.en: A card catalogue is a system for organizing information about the books and other materials in a library, consisting of cards with information on them that are arranged in a particular order.

words.ex: He added the bibliography at the end of his report.
words.ex_cn: 他在报告末尾添加了参考书目。
words.en: A bibliography is a list of the books and articles that have been used by someone when writing a particular book or article.

words.tr:
n. 插图说明；标题；字幕
v. 加上说明；加上标题；加上字幕
words.ex: The photo has a caption that says 'Happy birthday'.
words.ex_cn: 这张照片有一个标题，写着‘生日快乐’。
words.en: A caption is a short piece of text under a picture in a book, magazine, or newspaper that describes the picture or explains what is happening in it.

words.tr:
n. 倒塌；崩溃；暴跌；
v. 倒塌；崩溃；
words.ex: The collapse of the old bridge caused many problems.
words.ex_cn: 这座旧桥的倒塌引起了诸多问题。
words.en: If a building or other structure collapses, it falls down very suddenly.

words.tr: n. 崩溃；故障；细目分类；
words.ex: The stress led to a breakdown.
words.ex_cn: 压力导致了崩溃。
words.en: A breakdown is a failure of a system, machine, or relationship, or a sudden collapse in someone's mental health.

words.ex: A passer-by helped the old man cross the street.
words.ex_cn: 一位路人帮老人过马路。
words.en: A passer-by is a person who is walking past something, especially when something unusual is happening.

words.ex: The pedestrian crossed the street at the zebra crossing.
words.ex_cn: 行人在斑马线处过马路。
words.en: A pedestrian is a person who is walking in a city, town, or village, especially along a pavement or in a pedestrian area.

words.tr:
n. 通勤；
v. 通勤；
words.ex: His daily commute takes an hour by train.
words.ex_cn: 他每天的通勤坐火车要一个小时。
words.en: If you commute, you travel a long distance every day between your home and your place of work.

words.tr:
n. 经常重复的评价（或抱怨）；叠句；
v. 克制；
words.ex: His constant refrain is that the food is too expensive.
words.ex_cn: 他经常抱怨食物太贵。
words.en: If you refrain from doing something, you deliberately do not do it.

words.ex: He tries to restrain his anger.
words.ex_cn: 他努力克制自己的愤怒。
words.en: If you restrain someone, you stop them from doing what they intended or wanted to do, usually by using your physical strength.

words.ex: The law constrains companies from polluting rivers.
words.ex_cn: 法律约束公司不得污染河流。
words.en: To constrain someone or something means to limit their development or force them to behave in a particular way.

words.ex: He tried to curb his horse with the reins.
words.ex_cn: 他试图用缰绳勒住马。
words.en: If you curb something, you control it and keep it within limits.

words.ex: The faculty of engineering has many labs.
words.ex_cn: 工程学院有许多实验室。
words.en: A faculty is a group of departments in a university or college that specialize in a particular subject or group of subjects, or the teachers in such a group.

words.ex: The dean gave a speech at the graduation ceremony.
words.ex_cn: 院长在毕业典礼上发表了演讲。
words.en: A dean is a senior official in a college or university, who is in charge of a faculty or department or a group of students.

words.ex: The chancellor announced a new tax policy.
words.ex_cn: 大臣宣布了一项新的税收政策。
words.en: A chancellor is the head of the government in some countries, or a high-ranking official in a university or other institution.

words.ex: He starts his new class in the fall semester.
words.ex_cn: 他在秋季学期开始他的新课程。
words.en: A semester is one of the two periods that the school or college year is divided into, especially in the United States and Canada.

words.tr:
n. 纪律；学科；科目；训练；惩戒；
v. 约束自己；
words.ex: The teacher enforced discipline in the classroom.
words.ex_cn: 老师在教室里维持纪律。
words.en: Discipline is the practice of making people obey rules or standards of behaviour, and punishing them when they do not.

words.tr: n. 自助餐厅；自助食堂；
words.ex: We ate lunch in the school cafeteria.
words.ex_cn: 我们在学校自助餐厅吃午饭。
words.en: A cafeteria is a type of food service location within an institution in which there is little or no waiting staff table service, whether a restaurant or within an institution such as a large office building or school; a school dining location is also referred to as a dining hall or canteen (in British English).

words.ex: He is interested in linguistic patterns in children.
words.ex_cn: 他对儿童的语言模式感兴趣。
words.en: Relating to language or linguistics.

words.tr: adj. 人口统计的；人口的；
words.ex: The survey collected demographic data like age and income.
words.ex_cn: 这项调查收集了年龄和收入等人口统计数据。
words.en: Relating to the structure of populations.

words.tr: n. 修辞学；花言巧语；华丽的文辞；
words.ex: He studied rhetoric to improve his speaking skills.
words.ex_cn: 他学习修辞学以提高自己的演讲能力。
words.en: Rhetoric is the art or study of using language effectively and persuasively.

words.ex: He turned his head to avert the accident.
words.ex_cn: 他转过头去避免了事故。
words.en: If you avert something unpleasant, you prevent it from happening.

words.ex: He tries to invert the numbers to find the answer.
words.ex_cn: 他试图将数字倒过来以找到答案。
words.en: To invert something means to turn it upside down or to reverse its position, order, or relationship.

words.ex: He converts old paper into new notebooks.
words.ex_cn: 他把旧纸张转换成新笔记本。
words.en: To change something into a different form or to change someone's beliefs, especially their religious beliefs.

words.tr: adj. 不同的；多种多样的；
words.ex: The class has diverse students from many countries.
words.ex_cn: 这个班级有来自许多国家的不同学生。
words.en: If a group or range of things is diverse, it is made up of a wide variety of things.

words.tr:
n. 反面；
v. 使倒转；（使）倒车；撤销；
words.ex: The reverse of the coin has a picture of a tree.
words.ex_cn: 硬币的反面有一棵树的图案。
words.en: If you reverse the order of a set of things, you arrange them in the opposite order, so that the first thing comes last.

words.ex: He believed his destiny was to become a doctor.
words.ex_cn: 他相信自己的命运是成为一名医生。
words.en: Destiny is the force which some people believe controls the things that happen to you in your life.

words.ex: He lost his fortune in the stock market.
words.ex_cn: 他在股市中失去了他的财产。
words.en: A large amount of money or assets; chance or luck as an external force in human affairs.

words.tr:
n. 厄运；毁灭；死亡
v. 注定；判决
words.ex: The old prophecy spoke of doom for the kingdom.
words.ex_cn: 古老的预言说这个王国将遭遇厄运。
words.en: Doom is a terrible fate or destiny that you cannot avoid, especially death or destruction.

words.tr:
n. 补助金；授予物；
v. 承认；授予；允许；
words.ex: The university received a grant for scientific research.
words.ex_cn: 这所大学收到了一笔用于科学研究的补助金。
words.en: If someone in authority grants you something, or if something is granted to you, you are allowed to have it or do it.

words.tr: v. 授权；命名；给...权利（或资格）
words.ex: This book entitles you to a free gift.
words.ex_cn: 这本书使你有资格获得一份免费礼物。
words.en: If you are entitled to something, you have the right to have it or do it.

words.ex: The distance between the two towns is 10 kilometers.
words.ex_cn: 两个城镇之间的距离是10公里。
words.en: The amount of space between two places or things.

words.ex: The company wants to innovate its production process.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司想改革它的生产流程。
words.en: To innovate means to introduce changes and new ideas in the way something is done or made.

words.ex: I intend to go to the park tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 我打算明天去公园。
words.en: If you intend to do something, you have decided or planned to do it.

words.tr:
adj. 成熟的；
v. 成熟；
words.ex: He is a mature student who works full-time.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位成熟的学生，全职工作。
words.en: When something or someone matures, they become fully grown or developed. In finance, a mature investment is one that has reached the end of its term and is ready to be paid out.

words.tr:
adj. 军事的；军用的；
n. 军队；武装力量；
words.ex: The military base is near the border.
words.ex_cn: 军事基地靠近边境。
words.en: relating to or characteristic of soldiers or armed forces

words.ex: He flipped the pancake with a spatula.
words.ex_cn: 他用铲子快速翻转了煎饼。
words.en: To flip something means to turn it over quickly one or more times, or to make something do this.

words.ex: She wore a dress for the occasion.
words.ex_cn: 她为了这个特殊场合穿了一条裙子。
words.en: An occasion is a particular time when something happens, or a special event.

words.ex: The rainbow is a natural phenomenon.
words.ex_cn: 彩虹是一种自然现象。
words.en: A phenomenon is something that is observed to happen or exist, especially something that is unusual or interesting.

words.tr:
n. 框架；结构；骨架；模式；
v. 表达；陷害；
words.ex: The picture is in a wooden frame.
words.ex_cn: 这幅画在一个木制框架里。
words.en: A frame is a structure that forms a border or support for something, such as a picture or a window. It can also refer to the process of making or constructing something, or the act of falsely incriminating someone.

words.ex: He concluded that the experiment failed.
words.ex_cn: 他得出结论说实验失败了。
words.en: If you conclude that something is true, you decide that it is true using the facts you know as a basis.

words.tr:
v. 注册；登记；
n. 登记簿；
words.ex: He will register for the course next week.
words.ex_cn: 他下周会注册这门课程。
words.en: If you register something, you officially record it or list it.

words.tr:
n. 避难所；庇护所；
v. 庇护；遮蔽；
words.ex: The refugees found shelter in a small building.
words.ex_cn: 难民们在一个小建筑里找到了避难所。
words.en: A shelter is a small building or covered place which is made to protect people from bad weather or danger.

words.tr:
adj. 固体的；坚固的；可靠的；
n. 固体；
words.ex: Ice is a solid form of water.
words.ex_cn: 冰是水的固体形式。
words.en: A solid substance or object stays the same shape whether it is in a container or not.

words.tr: n. 效用；实用；公用事业；
words.ex: The utility of this tool is very high.
words.ex_cn: 这个工具的效用非常高。
words.en: Utility refers to the state of being useful, profitable, or beneficial.

words.ex: They enclose the garden with a wooden fence.
words.ex_cn: 他们用木栅栏把花园围起来。
words.en: If you enclose something with a letter, you put it in the same envelope as the letter.

words.ex: He put the letter in an envelope.
words.ex_cn: 他把信装进了一个信封。
words.en: An envelope is a flat, usually rectangular or square, paper container for a letter, which you seal before you send it by post.

words.tr: v. 参军；入伍；谋求（某人的帮助）
words.ex: He wants to enlist in the army.
words.ex_cn: 他想参军。
words.en: To enlist means to join the military, or to get someone else to join the military. It can also mean to get support or help from someone for a particular purpose.

words.ex: She entrusted her keys to her friend.
words.ex_cn: 她把钥匙托付给了朋友。
words.en: If you entrust something important to someone or entrust them with it, you give them the responsibility of looking after it or dealing with it.

words.ex: The coach endorses the new player.
words.ex_cn: 教练支持这位新球员。
words.en: If you endorse someone or something, you say publicly that you support or approve of them.

words.ex: The truck runs on diesel.
words.ex_cn: 这辆卡车使用柴油运行。
words.en: Diesel is a type of heavy oil used as fuel in diesel engines.

words.ex: The car has a strong engine.
words.ex_cn: 这辆车有一个强劲的发动机。
words.en: An engine is a machine that converts energy into mechanical force and motion.

words.ex: The engine has four cylinders.
words.ex_cn: 发动机有四个气缸。
words.en: A cylinder is a geometric figure with straight parallel sides and a circular or oval cross section.

words.tr:
n. 刹车；制动器
v. 刹车
words.ex: He pressed the brake to stop the car.
words.ex_cn: 他踩了刹车来停车。
words.en: A brake is a device in a vehicle that makes it go slower or stop.

words.ex: He used a jack to lift the car.
words.ex_cn: 他用千斤顶把车顶了起来。
words.en: A jack is a device for lifting heavy objects, especially one for raising the axle of a motor vehicle so that a wheel can be changed or removed.

words.ex: The computer uses a buffer to store data temporarily.
words.ex_cn: 计算机使用缓冲区临时存储数据。
words.en: A buffer is something that prevents something else from being harmed or that reduces the impact of something.

words.ex: He pressed the pedal to speed up the bike.
words.ex_cn: 他踩下踏板让自行车加速。
words.en: A pedal is a lever that you press with your foot in order to control a vehicle or machine.

words.ex: Washing hands can kill germs.
words.ex_cn: 洗手可以杀死病菌。
words.en: A germ is a very small organism that causes disease.

words.ex: The doctor gave me an antibiotic for my infection.
words.ex_cn: 医生给我开了抗菌素治疗感染。
words.en: A substance that can kill or inhibit the growth of bacteria and other microorganisms.

words.ex: He got a vaccine last week.
words.ex_cn: 他上周打了疫苗。
words.en: A vaccine is a substance containing a virus or bacterium in a form that is not harmful, given to a person or animal to prevent them from getting the disease that the virus or bacterium causes.

words.ex: The virus can infect people quickly.
words.ex_cn: 这种病毒能迅速感染人。
words.en: To infect someone or something means to cause them to have a disease or illness.

words.tr: adj. 传染性的；有感染力的；
words.ex: The flu is contagious and spreads easily.
words.ex_cn: 流感具有传染性，容易传播。
words.en: A contagious disease can be caught by touching someone who has the disease or by touching an infected object or by breathing in infected air.

words.tr: adj. 有免疫力的；免疫的；不受影响的；
words.ex: Children are immune to this disease after vaccination.
words.ex_cn: 儿童接种疫苗后对这种疾病有免疫力。
words.en: If you are immune to a particular disease, you cannot be affected by it. If you are immune to something such as criticism, it does not affect you.

words.ex: The epidemic spread quickly across the country.
words.ex_cn: 这种流行病迅速蔓延到全国。
words.en: An epidemic is a large number of cases of an infectious disease occurring at the same time.

words.ex: He can articulate his ideas clearly.
words.ex_cn: 他能清楚地表达自己的想法。
words.en: If you describe someone as articulate, you mean that they are able to express their thoughts and ideas easily and clearly.

words.tr: adj. 雄辩的；有口才的；有说服力的
words.ex: He gave an eloquent speech at the ceremony.
words.ex_cn: 他在仪式上发表了富有感染力的演讲。
words.en: If you describe someone as eloquent, you mean that they are able to express their ideas and opinions well, so that other people understand them and are influenced by them.

words.ex: He is proficient in playing the piano.
words.ex_cn: 他弹钢琴很熟练。
words.en: If you are proficient in something, you can do it well because you have learned how to do it.

words.tr: n. 专门知识；专门技能；
words.ex: His expertise in computers helps the team solve problems.
words.ex_cn: 他在计算机方面的专门知识帮助团队解决问题。
words.en: Expertise is special skill or knowledge that is acquired by training, study, or practice.

words.tr:
adj. 客观的；
n. 目标；目的；
words.ex: He gave an objective opinion about the movie.
words.ex_cn: 他对这部电影给出了一个客观的看法。
words.en: An objective is something that you plan to do or achieve.

words.ex: He stayed neutral in the argument.
words.ex_cn: 他在争论中保持中立。
words.en: If you say that someone is neutral, you mean that they do not support or help either side in a disagreement, competition, or war.

words.tr:
adj. 公平的；相当大的；合理的；
n. 集市；
words.ex: The teacher gave a fair grade to every student.
words.ex_cn: 老师给每个学生都给了一个公平的分数。
words.en: Fair means treating people equally without favouritism or discrimination.

words.ex: He was imprisoned for stealing.
words.ex_cn: 他因偷窃而被监禁。
words.en: To put someone in prison or keep them as a prisoner.

words.tr: adj. 即将发生的；临近的；
words.ex: An imminent storm is coming soon.
words.ex_cn: 一场即将发生的风暴很快就要来了。
words.en: If you say that something is imminent, especially something unpleasant, you mean it is almost certain to happen very soon.

words.ex: He imparts knowledge to his students every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天向学生传授知识。
words.en: If you impart information to people, you tell it to them. To impart a particular quality to something means to give it that quality.

words.ex: The injury impaired his ability to walk.
words.ex_cn: 这次受伤损害了他走路的能力。
words.en: If something impairs something such as an ability or the way something works, it damages it or makes it worse.

words.ex: His insight helped the team solve the problem.
words.ex_cn: 他的洞察力帮助团队解决了问题。
words.en: If you gain insight or an insight into a complex situation or problem, you gain an accurate and deep understanding of it.

words.ex: His intellect helps him solve difficult problems.
words.ex_cn: 他的智力帮助他解决难题。
words.en: The ability to understand and think in a logical way about things.

words.tr: adj. 基本的；基础的；根本的；
words.ex: Water is a fundamental need for life.
words.ex_cn: 水是生命的基本需求。
words.en: You use fundamental to describe things, activities, and principles that are very important or essential. They affect the basic nature of other things or are the most important element upon which other things depend.

words.tr: adj. 根本的；彻底的；激进的；
words.ex: The government made radical changes to the education system.
words.ex_cn: 政府对教育系统进行了根本性的改革。
words.en: A radical change or difference is very big and important.

words.ex: The basis of math is numbers.
words.ex_cn: 数学的基础是数字。
words.en: The underlying support or foundation for an idea, argument, or process.

words.ex: Water is indispensable for life.
words.ex_cn: 水对生命是必不可少的。
words.en: Absolutely necessary or essential.

words.ex: The rain persisted all day.
words.ex_cn: 雨持续了一整天。
words.en: If you persist in doing something, you continue to do it even though it is difficult or other people are against it.

words.ex: He persevered despite many failures.
words.ex_cn: 尽管多次失败，他仍然坚持不懈。
words.en: If you persevere with something, you keep trying to do it and do not give up, even though it is difficult.

words.ex: She insists on going home now.
words.ex_cn: 她坚决要求现在回家。
words.en: If you insist on doing something, you keep doing it, even though it is difficult or other people are against it.

words.tr:
n. 内部；
adj. 内部的；
words.ex: The interior of the house is very cozy.
words.ex_cn: 房子的内部非常舒适。
words.en: The interior of something is the inside part of it.

words.ex: The internal parts of the machine need repair.
words.ex_cn: 机器的内部零件需要修理。
words.en: Internal is used to describe things that exist or happen inside a particular person, object, or place.

words.ex: We played chess indoors because it was raining.
words.ex_cn: 因为下雨，我们在室内下棋。
words.en: Located, done, or used inside a building.

words.ex: He stood in the midst of the crowd.
words.ex_cn: 他站在人群中间。
words.en: The middle part or point of something.

words.ex: Birds migrate south in winter.
words.ex_cn: 鸟类在冬天迁徙到南方。
words.en: If people migrate, they move from one place to another, especially in order to find work or to live somewhere for a short time.

words.ex: He wants to emigrate to Canada for a better life.
words.ex_cn: 他想移民到加拿大过更好的生活。
words.en: To leave one's own country in order to settle permanently in another.

words.ex: They want to immigrate to Canada for a better life.
words.ex_cn: 他们想移民到加拿大过更好的生活。
words.en: To come to live permanently in a foreign country.

words.ex: The tribe lives in a primitive hut.
words.ex_cn: 这个部落住在原始的小屋里。
words.en: Belonging to a very early period in the history of the world, or to a time before modern things existed.

words.tr:
adj. 最初的；开始的；
n. 首字母；
words.ex: This is the initial plan for the project.
words.ex_cn: 这是这个项目的最初计划。
words.en: The first letter of a name or word, used to represent the whole name or word.

words.ex: The origin of this tradition is unknown.
words.ex_cn: 这个传统的起源不明。
words.en: The origin of something is the point or place where it begins, or the cause from which it arises.

words.tr: n. 道德规范；伦理标准；
words.ex: The company follows a strong ethic of honesty.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司遵循诚实的道德规范。
words.en: An ethic is a moral principle or set of moral principles that guides the behavior of a person or group, especially in a professional context.

words.tr:
adj. 道德的；道义上的；
n. 寓意；
words.ex: It is a moral duty to tell the truth.
words.ex_cn: 说实话是一种道德责任。
words.en: Concerned with the principles of right and wrong behavior and the goodness or badness of human character.

words.ex: He always follows the principle of honesty.
words.ex_cn: 他总是遵循诚实的原则。
words.en: A principle is a basic idea or rule that explains or controls how something happens or works.

words.tr:
v. 抗议；
n. 抗议活动；
words.ex: The students protest against the new school rules.
words.ex_cn: 学生们抗议新的校规。
words.en: A protest is the act of saying or showing publicly that you object to something.

words.tr: n. 对抗；对立；敌对状态（行为）
words.ex: There is antagonism between the two neighbors.
words.ex_cn: 这两个邻居之间有敌意。
words.en: Antagonism is a strong feeling of dislike or opposition towards someone or something.

words.ex: Wear a helmet to counteract the risk of head injury.
words.ex_cn: 戴头盔以对抗头部受伤的风险。
words.en: If you counteract something, you reduce its effect by doing something that produces an opposite effect.

words.ex: Rare birds can be seen in this forest.
words.ex_cn: 这种森林里可以看到稀有的鸟类。
words.en: Something that is rare is not common and is therefore interesting or valuable.

words.tr: adj. 缺乏的；不足的；稀有的；
words.ex: Water is scarce in the desert.
words.ex_cn: 沙漠里水很缺乏。
words.en: If something is scarce, there is not enough of it.

words.tr:
n. 抵制；拒绝参加；
v. 抵制；拒绝参加；
words.ex: The students organized a boycott of the unfair school rule.
words.ex_cn: 学生们组织了对这项不公平校规的抵制。
words.en: If a country, group, or person boycotts a country, organization, or activity, they refuse to be involved with it in any way because they disapprove of it.

words.ex: He reject the job offer.
words.ex_cn: 他拒绝了这份工作邀请。
words.en: If you reject something such as a proposal, a request, or an offer, you do not accept it or you do not agree to it.

words.tr:
v. 防止；战斗；抑制；
n. 战斗；
words.ex: The new law aims to combat pollution.
words.ex_cn: 这项新法律旨在防止污染。
words.en: Combat refers to fighting, especially during a war. It can also mean to try to stop something harmful from happening or increasing.

words.ex: He has a monopoly on selling ice cream in this town.
words.ex_cn: 他在这座小镇上垄断了冰淇淋的销售。
words.en: If a company, person, or state has a monopoly on something such as an industry, they have complete control over it, so that it is impossible for others to become involved in it.

words.ex: He works in retail at a small store.
words.ex_cn: 他在一家小店从事零售工作。
words.en: The sale of goods to the public in relatively small quantities for use or consumption rather than for resale.

words.tr:
adj. 批发的；
n. 成批出售；
adv. 大批地；
words.ex: He buys clothes at wholesale prices.
words.ex_cn: 他以批发价购买衣服。
words.en: Wholesale is the business of buying and selling goods in large quantities, especially for resale to retailers.

words.ex: He wants to rid his house of clutter.
words.ex_cn: 他想摆脱家里的杂乱。
words.en: To rid someone or something of something unwanted or harmful means to remove it completely from them.

words.ex: He used a long rod to reach the top shelf.
words.ex_cn: 他用一根长杆够到顶层架子。
words.en: A rod is a long, thin, straight bar, especially one made of wood or metal.

words.ex: The math proof requires rigor.
words.ex_cn: 这个数学证明需要严谨。
words.en: Rigor is a situation in which people are made to follow rules in a very strict way.

words.tr: adj. 刻板的；坚硬的；严格的；
words.ex: He has a rigid attitude toward rules.
words.ex_cn: 他对规则的态度很刻板。
words.en: not able to be changed or adapted; not able to be bent or moved; stiff

words.ex: The sailors cleaned the stern of the boat.
words.ex_cn: 水手们打扫了船尾。
words.en: If you describe someone or their behavior as stern, you mean that they are severe or strict.

words.tr: v. 吞食；吞噬；狼吞虎咽地吃；如饥似渴地看
words.ex: The dog devoured the meat quickly.
words.ex_cn: 狗很快地把肉吃光了。
words.en: To eat something quickly and eagerly, especially because you are very hungry; to destroy something quickly and completely.

words.tr:
n. 废墟；
v. 破坏；
words.ex: The old temple is now a ruin.
words.ex_cn: 这座古老的寺庙现在已成为废墟。
words.en: Ruin means the physical destruction or disintegration of something or the state of disintegrating or being destroyed.

words.ex: The earthquake devastated the small town.
words.ex_cn: 地震摧毁了这个小镇。
words.en: To devastate means to destroy or ruin something completely, or to cause someone to feel extreme sadness or shock.

words.ex: The stain on the carpet is a mar.
words.ex_cn: 地毯上的污渍是一个污点。
words.en: To mar something means to spoil or damage it.

words.tr:
v. 密谋；激起…的兴趣
n. 阴谋诡计；密谋策划
words.ex: They intrigue to take over the company.
words.ex_cn: 他们密谋接管这家公司。
words.en: If something intrigues you, it interests you a lot because it seems strange or mysterious.

words.ex: They conspire to cheat on the test.
words.ex_cn: 他们密谋在考试中作弊。
words.en: If two or more people or groups conspire to do something illegal or harmful, they make a secret agreement to do it.

words.ex: The police discovered a scheme to steal money.
words.ex_cn: 警方发现了一个偷钱的阴谋。
words.en: A scheme is a plan or arrangement, especially one produced by a government or other organization, or a secret plan to do something, especially something illegal or dishonest.

words.ex: The school used to segregate students by race.
words.ex_cn: 这所学校过去按种族隔离学生。
words.en: To segregate means to separate one group of people, animals, or things from another, especially because they are of different types or belong to different categories.

words.tr: v. 隔离；使隔热；使隔音；使绝缘
words.ex: The walls insulate the house from cold air.
words.ex_cn: 墙壁将房子与冷空气隔离开。
words.en: To insulate something means to protect it from heat, cold, noise, or electricity by covering it in a material that prevents it from passing through.

words.ex: The hospital will isolate the patient to stop the spread.
words.ex_cn: 医院将隔离这名病人以防止传播。
words.en: To isolate someone or something means to separate them from other people or things, often in order to protect them or to prevent the spread of something harmful.

words.ex: The phone has a silicon chip inside.
words.ex_cn: 这部手机内部有一个硅芯片。
words.en: Silicon is a chemical element with the symbol Si and atomic number 14. It is a hard, brittle crystalline solid with a blue-grey metallic lustre, and is a tetravalent metalloid and semiconductor.

words.ex: Plants need nitrogen to grow.
words.ex_cn: 植物需要氮来生长。
words.en: A chemical element with the symbol N and atomic number 7. It is a colorless, odorless, tasteless gas that is the most plentiful element in Earth's atmosphere and is a constituent of all living tissues.

words.ex: Plants release oxygen into the air.
words.ex_cn: 植物向空气中释放氧气。
words.en: A colourless, odourless reactive gas, the chemical element of atomic number 8 and the life-supporting component of the air.

words.ex: Rust is an oxide of iron.
words.ex_cn: 铁锈是铁的氧化物。
words.en: An oxide is a chemical compound that contains at least one oxygen atom and one other element in its chemical formula.

words.ex: Carbon dioxide makes the air warm.
words.ex_cn: 二氧化碳使空气变暖。
words.en: A compound containing two atoms of oxygen combined with another element or group.

words.ex: The old bike has rust on its chain.
words.ex_cn: 这辆旧自行车的链条上有锈。
words.en: Rust is a reddish-brown substance that forms on the surface of iron or steel when they are exposed to air and moisture, causing them to corrode.

words.tr:
n. 石油化学制品
adj. 石化的
words.ex: The factory makes petrochemicals from oil.
words.ex_cn: 这家工厂从石油中生产石油化工产品。
words.en: A petrochemical is a chemical obtained from petroleum and natural gas.

words.tr:
n. 合金
v. 把…铸成合金
words.ex: He made a strong alloy from copper and zinc.
words.ex_cn: 他用铜和锌制造了一种坚固的合金。
words.en: An alloy is a metal made by combining two or more metallic elements, especially to give greater strength or resistance to corrosion.

words.ex: The shirt is made of synthetic fabric.
words.ex_cn: 这件衬衫是合成纤维制成的。
words.en: Synthetic products are made from chemicals or artificial substances rather than from natural ones.

words.ex: The table is made of a composite material.
words.ex_cn: 这张桌子是由一种合成材料制成的。
words.en: A composite is something that is made up of several different parts or materials.

words.ex: The alcohol is volatile and evaporates quickly.
words.ex_cn: 酒精是易挥发的，会迅速蒸发。
words.en: A volatile situation or person is one that is likely to change suddenly and unexpectedly, especially by getting worse.

words.ex: The ball keeps moving because of inertia.
words.ex_cn: 球因为惯性继续移动。
words.en: Inertia is the tendency of a physical object to continue moving in a straight line at a constant speed, or to stay at rest, unless it is acted upon by a force.

words.ex: Running a business entails hard work.
words.ex_cn: 经营企业必然需要努力工作。
words.en: If one thing entails another, it involves it or causes it.

words.ex: We celebrate my birthday with cake and friends.
words.ex_cn: 我们用蛋糕和朋友庆祝我的生日。
words.en: To celebrate means to mark a special day, event, or occasion with festivities or ceremonies. It can also mean to praise or honor someone or something.

words.tr: adj. 一致的；始终如一的；
words.ex: His answers are consistent with the data.
words.ex_cn: 他的答案与数据一致。
words.en: Someone who is consistent always behaves in the same way, has the same attitudes towards people or things, or achieves the same level of success in something.

words.ex: The company plans to recruit new staff next month.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司计划下个月招聘新员工。
words.en: To recruit means to enlist someone in the armed forces or to persuade someone to join a company, organization, or group.

words.ex: Farmers cultivate rice in the fields.
words.ex_cn: 农民在田里种植水稻。
words.en: To cultivate land means to prepare it and grow crops on it. To cultivate a particular quality, skill, or attitude means to try hard to develop it and make it stronger.

words.ex: The train's destination is Beijing.
words.ex_cn: 这列火车的目的地是北京。
words.en: The place to which someone or something is going or being sent.

words.ex: The children were exposed to cold weather without coats.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们在没有外套的情况下遭受了寒冷天气。
words.en: To expose something means to uncover it so that it can be seen, or to make it known or public.

words.ex: They cooperate to finish the project on time.
words.ex_cn: 他们合作以按时完成项目。
words.en: If you cooperate with someone, you work with them or help them for a particular purpose.

words.ex: The loud noise gave her a sudden fright.
words.ex_cn: 巨大的噪音让她吓了一跳。
words.en: A sudden intense feeling of fear.

words.ex: The slow internet frustrates me.
words.ex_cn: 慢速的网络让我感到沮丧。
words.en: If something frustrates you, it upsets or angers you because you are unable to deal with the problems it creates.

words.tr:
v. 保证；确保；
n. 保证；保证书；
words.ex: The store guarantees a refund if you are not happy.
words.ex_cn: 如果你不满意，商店保证退款。
words.en: A guarantee is a formal promise that certain conditions will be fulfilled, especially that a product will be repaired or replaced if it is not of a specified quality.

words.ex: The wound will heal in a few days.
words.ex_cn: 伤口几天后就会愈合。
words.en: To make or become healthy or whole again; to cure or recover from an injury or illness.

words.tr: v. 使留下深刻印象；使铭记；
words.ex: His speech impressed everyone in the room.
words.ex_cn: 他的演讲给在场的每个人留下了深刻印象。
words.en: If someone or something impresses you, you feel great admiration for them.

words.ex: The house is situated near the river.
words.ex_cn: 这所房子位于河边。
words.en: If something is situated in a particular place or position, it is in that place or position.

words.tr: adj. 卓越的；极好的；明亮的；灿烂的；
words.ex: He gave a brilliant answer to the math question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这道数学题给出了卓越的回答。
words.en: A brilliant person, idea, or performance is extremely clever or skilful.

words.ex: The desert has little vegetation.
words.ex_cn: 这个沙漠植被很少。
words.en: Vegetation refers to plants in general, or the plants that are found in a particular area. It can also refer to a life that is dull or inactive, often due to illness or lack of exercise.

words.ex: The shrub grows near the fence.
words.ex_cn: 这丛灌木长在篱笆附近。
words.en: A shrub is a woody plant which is smaller than a tree and has several main stems arising at or near the ground.

words.ex: The rose has a sharp thorn.
words.ex_cn: 玫瑰有一根尖刺。
words.en: A thorn is a sharp, pointed projection on the stem or other part of a plant.

words.ex: She dried the herb to make tea.
words.ex_cn: 她晒干了这种药草来泡茶。
words.en: A plant or a part of a plant that is used for its medicinal, savory, or aromatic qualities.

words.ex: The old man walks with a cane.
words.ex_cn: 这位老人拄着藤杖走路。
words.en: A cane is a long, thin stick that you can use to help you walk, or it is a stick used for punishing people by hitting them. It is also a tall, hard plant like bamboo, from which sugar is made.

words.tr:
n. 茎；词干；
v. 起源于(~ from)；
words.ex: The flower grows on a long green stem.
words.ex_cn: 花长在一根长长的绿色茎上。
words.en: The main body or stalk of a plant or shrub, typically rising above ground but occasionally subterranean; to stop or restrict (the flow of something).

words.ex: Children must obey their parents.
words.ex_cn: 孩子必须遵守父母的规定。
words.en: To obey means to do what you are told or expected to do according to a rule, law, or someone with authority over you.

words.ex: You must comply with the rules.
words.ex_cn: 你必须遵守规则。
words.en: To act in accordance with a wish or command.

words.ex: He will submit his homework tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他明天会提交他的作业。
words.en: To yield or surrender (oneself) to the will or authority of another.

words.tr:
n. 金额；总数；
v. 概括；
words.ex: The sum of the bill is fifty dollars.
words.ex_cn: 账单的金额是五十美元。
words.en: A sum is an amount of money, or the total amount of two or more amounts of money added together.

words.ex: He gave a summary of the story at the end.
words.ex_cn: 他在结尾对故事做了总结。
words.en: A summary is a brief statement or account of the main points of something.

words.ex: The climbers reached the summit of the mountain.
words.ex_cn: 登山者到达了山顶。
words.en: The highest point of a hill or mountain; a meeting between heads of government.

words.tr:
n. 更新；
v. 更新；升级；
words.ex: The app sent me a new update.
words.ex_cn: 应用程序给我发送了一个新更新。
words.en: To make something more modern or up to date, especially by adding new information or changing its design or style.

words.ex: They will renovate the old house next month.
words.ex_cn: 他们下个月将翻新那栋老房子。
words.en: To renovate means to restore something to a good state of repair or to make it as good as new.

words.ex: He will restore the old bike.
words.ex_cn: 他将修复这辆旧自行车。
words.en: To restore something means to bring it back to its original condition or to a state of health, efficiency, or good management.

words.ex: He revised his answer to make it correct.
words.ex_cn: 他修正了他的答案，使其正确。
words.en: To revise something means to alter or amend it, especially in order to correct or improve it.

words.ex: He will renew his passport next week.
words.ex_cn: 他下周会更新他的护照。
words.en: To renew something means to begin it again or to make it new again.
